signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Repricing
signals.text: CHF/JPY trades at 188.16, pressured by divergent weekly G10 currency returns. JPY leads the G10 basket with an average weekly gain of +1.449% across 7 pairs, while CHF lags the table with a weekly decline of -0.762% across 6 pairs, yielding an active bilateral spread of 2.211%. JPY strength persists despite an accommodative real policy rate of -1.45% relative to Swiss real rates at -1.24%, while BoJ policy at 1.25% maintains a +125bp nominal policy advantage over the SNB at 0.00%. Options skew confirms sustained downside protection demand across yen crosses, with EUR/JPY 25d RR at -2.63 and USD/JPY 25d RR at -2.61. Spot remains stretched below its BEER fair-value estimate of 195.25 (z = -2.01σ). Trade bias: Bearish CHF/JPY, momentum favors yen outperformance across funding crosses. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions release at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Cross-asset equity recovery drives renewed carry demand and compresses the bilateral gap below 1.20%.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Energy Geopolitics + Retail Extreme
signals.text: USD/CAD holds at 1.4186, trading above its SMA20 at 1.3958, SMA50 at 1.3951, and SMA200 at 1.3846. WTI crude trades up +0.48% at $89.80 per barrel following stalled US-Iran diplomatic talks and reaffirmed sanctions enforcement. Retail positioning is heavily skewed with 95% short against 5% long, running contrary to the prevailing technical uptrend and the underlying +160bp OIS carry spread (SOFR 3.90% vs CORRA 2.30%). COT positioning reflects institutional caution with Leveraged Funds net short CAD by -49,123 contracts (pctl 69, WoW -7,719), setting up retail squeeze risk if spot extends through recent highs. MOVE index at 106.6 marks the 98th percentile of its trailing year while VIX sits at 16.0 (27th percentile), reflecting fixed-income and policy rate volatility that sustains the greenback's carry appeal. Trade bias: Long USD/CAD, structural carry advantage and retail short-squeeze imbalance dominate. Catalyst: US Core PCE release at 12:30 UTC — 3.3% y/y expected. Risk: Sustained oil breakout above $95.00 improves Canadian terms of trade and breaks technical support at 1.3950.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Core Inflation Rebound vs Real Yield Drag
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1355, holding below its daily SMA cluster of SMA20 at 1.1514, SMA50 at 1.1536, and SMA200 at 1.1620. Preliminary French September CPI accelerated to +3.0% y/y versus +2.8% expected, while German August import prices advanced +1.0% m/m against +0.7% projected. Upbeat European inflation prints contrast with widening rate headwinds, as US 5Y yields rose +23bp over 5 sessions (FRED, as of Sep 28) entirely through real yields (+23bp real vs +0bp breakeven). The Fed at 4.00% maintains a +135bp policy rate advantage at 2.65%, reinforced by a +146bp OIS carry premium favoring the dollar (SOFR 3.90% vs €STR 2.44%). Speculative positioning remains net short EUR among Leveraged Funds at -58,805 contracts (pctl 19, WoW -7,450), indicating that European inflation beats are being absorbed as late-cycle stagflation rather than aggressive ECB tightening. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, policy divergence and real yield differentials constrain rallies below 1.1515. Catalyst: German Preliminary CPI at 12:00 UTC — 2.7% y/y expected. Risk: US Core PCE misses at 12:30 UTC, sparking a broad dollar correction toward 1.1500.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Dovish RBA Guidance vs Crowded Spec Long
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6974, breaking below its daily SMA20 at 0.7126, SMA50 at 0.7096, and SMA200 at 0.7029. Although the RBA raised the cash rate to 4.60%, forward guidance softened considerably, dampening expectations for subsequent rate hikes. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds hold an elevated net long of +55,684 contracts (pctl 81, z +0.92), while retail sentiment sits at 79% long. The 2Y yield spread between Australia and the US compressed by -22bp over the last 5 sessions to flat (+0bp), sharply reducing the Australian yield buffer despite a lingering -70bp AONIA-SOFR OIS carry advantage. With spot trading below the SMA200 threshold, long positioning faces liquidation pressure if global risk appetite deteriorates. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/USD, crowded speculative longs vulnerable to unwinding on neutral RBA path. Catalyst: RBA Financial Stability Review at 01:30 UTC. Risk: Sharp commodity advance lifts AUD/USD back above SMA200 resistance at 0.7030.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Volatility Disconnect + Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 156.79, positioned above its SMA20 at 156.13 but below the SMA50 at 158.38 and SMA200 at 158.46. One-month ATM implied volatility sits at 9.2% against 30-day realized volatility of 10.2%, creating a negative vol risk premium of -1.0% that highlights pricing complacency. Conversely, the 25-delta risk reversal prints at -2.61, indicating pronounced demand for downside yen-call protection. The Fed-BoJ carry spread remains wide at +275bp nominal (Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25%) and +267bp in OIS terms (SOFR 3.90% vs TONA 1.23%), containing spot pullbacks near 156.00 while the 160.00 handle continues to mark the key threshold associated with intervention awareness. Trade bias: Range-bound USD/JPY, carry support offsets heavy options downside hedging between 156.10 and 158.40. Catalyst: Tokyo CPI release at 23:30 UTC — Core forecast 1.9% y/y. Risk: Breakdown below SMA20 support at 156.13 accelerates downside hedging toward 154.50.
